significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish both a causal mechanism and a form-(iii) predictive law: reversing the objective installs an anti-aligned trait, while "the magnitude of the anti-trait predicts the magnitude of ordinary positive transfer" with approximate sign symmetry. This would fix expectations for an entire family of positive/inverse-training pairs and connect the behavioral phenomenon to the proposed gradient-alignment mechanism; Cloud et al., "Subliminal Learning: Language Models Transmit Behavioral Traits via Hidden Signals in Data" (arXiv:2507.14805), makes gradient alignment load-bearing to the current explanation, so sign symmetry directly discriminates that explanation rather than merely documenting another transferred trait. A negative result would rule out the simple sign-reversible account and show that ordinary subliminal transfer depends on asymmetric optimization dynamics, although it would not by itself identify the replacement mechanism; true and false therefore describe distinguishable, informative states. Topic-substitution check: deleting the sign reversal, anti-alignment, and symmetry relation leaves only a request to extend subliminal-learning research, which would not merit this score.

reach.justification: The named handle is a "practical, label-free inoculation" implemented through a "sign-flipped objective," and it is ex ante because it modifies a student before deployment using innocuous outputs from an undesirable teacher rather than diagnosing a trait after failure. Its symmetry claim also survives recalibration as a relation: after measuring ordinary transfer in another compatible model, it predicts the sign and approximate magnitude of inverse transfer, while "negative cosine" supplies a mechanistic diagnostic rather than merely a search procedure. The asserted scope covers multiple transferable traits and undesirable teachers but retains the stated same-base/model-family qualification; downstream uptake could include practitioners training or gating models, not just researchers analyzing subliminal channels. Topic-substitution check: the generic topic supplies neither this intervention nor its forward prediction, so the reach score comes from the claim-specific handle and action window.
